why: The student claims without any reason that assigning the boolean directly would act like the if; this is true for this code, but it does not give the output or say when the loop stops, so it is one correct but unjustified point (L1).

concepts.quote: isDone = (i % 5 == 0); would do the same as the if.
concepts.why: The claim is correct here because the loop exits right after isDone first becomes true, so it is never set back to false; but the student only asserts it and does not explain why the two are the same, so it does not reach L4 (predict a change).
Correctly stores the boolean result of a comparison straight into the variable, but does not apply this to the code's values.
Makes no claim about what % gives.
Makes no claim about how && is evaluated in the loop condition.
